title: What does one diagonal of a kite do to the other?
description: In a kite, two pairs of congruent triangles show that one diagonal bisects the two angles at its ends. It also cuts the other diagonal in half at a right angle. Keeko doubts that each diagonal cuts the other in half.
teaching_notes: One idea: the diagonal through the corners where equal sides meet bisects those angles and cuts the other diagonal in half at a right angle. Watch for students who think both diagonals of a kite cut each other in half.

source: In the kite ABCD, show that the diagonal BD (i) bisects ∠ABC and ∠ADC, (ii) bisects the diagonal AC, that is, AO = OC, and is perpendicular to it.
video_script.why: The child sees that congruent triangles on both sides of the diagonal show that it bisects two angles and cuts the other diagonal in half at a right angle.
video_script.substitution: the book's own kite ABCD with AB = BC and CD = DA, and its diagonals meeting at O
video_script.anchor: the kite ABCD of the book with its diagonals AC and BD crossing at O
video_script.wrong_answer: each diagonal cuts the other in half
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks each diagonal of a kite cuts the other in half, but only the diagonal BD cuts AC in half.
video_script.payoff_line: B D bisects both angles and cuts eigh C in half

final_answer.value: BD bisects ∠ABC and ∠ADC, and it cuts AC in half at right angles
final_answer.spoken: B D bisects angle eigh B C and angle eigh D C, and it cuts eigh C in half at right angles

hold_back: BD bisects ∠ABC and ∠ADC, and it cuts AC in half at right angles
never_show: AO = OC written for the diagonal BD
maths_rules: triangle ABD and triangle CBD: AB = CB, AD = CD, BD common, so they are congruent by SSS
angle ABD = angle CBD and angle ADB = angle CDB, so BD bisects angle ABC and angle ADC
triangle AOB and triangle COB: AB = CB, angle ABO = angle CBO, BO common, so they are congruent by SAS
AO = OC and angle AOB = angle COB
angle AOB + angle COB = 180, so each is 180 / 2 = 90
video_script.design: One idea: two pairs of congruent triangles prove everything about the diagonal. One kite stays on the board, and the triangles are coloured in turn.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a kite.
<bookmark mark='kite'/>In kite eigh B C D, eigh B equals B C, and C D equals D eigh.
<bookmark mark='diag'/>The two diagonals cross at a point called O.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What do you notice about the diagonals at O?

narration: <bookmark mark='bis'/>To bisect means to cut into two equal parts.
<bookmark mark='cong'/>Triangles that match exactly are called congruent.

narration: <bookmark mark='sides'/>Step one, eigh B equals C B, eigh D equals C D, and B D is common.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>By the side side side rule, triangle eigh B D is congruent to triangle C B D.

narration: <bookmark mark='b'/>Step two, matching angles are equal, so angle eigh B D equals angle C B D.
<bookmark mark='d'/>In the same way, angle eigh D B equals angle C D B.
The diagonal B D bisects both angles.

beats.on_screen: In ∆AOB and ∆COB: AB = CB, ∠ABO = ∠CBO, BO common, so ∆AOB ≅ ∆COB (two sides and the angle between); AO = OC

marks.ang: the angle between them lights up
marks.eq: eigh O equals O C is written

narration: <bookmark mark='sides'/>Step three, look at the small triangles eigh O B and C O B.
Eigh B equals C B, and B O is common.
<bookmark mark='ang'/>Angle eigh B O equals angle C B O.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>By the side angle side rule, they are congruent.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>Matching sides are equal, so eigh O equals O C.

marks.eq: angle A O B and angle C O B light up as equal
marks.line: A C is traced as a straight line

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step four, matching angles are equal, so angle eigh O B equals angle C O B.
<bookmark mark='line'/>They sit on the straight line eigh C, so together they make one hundred eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='ninety'/>One hundred eighty divided by two gives ninety degrees for each.
